newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EMV, MERKO, LEKS SEEK BOURSE LISTINGS.
newsitem.headline: EMV, MERKO, LEKS SEEK BOURSE LISTINGS.

text.p: The Tallinn stock exchange said on Thursday that construction companies EMV and Merko have applied to the main list of the bourse.
Leks Insurance has also applied to have its shares placed on the secondary list, the listing commission head of the bourse, Rain Semper, told Reuters.
EMV shares are traded on the free market of the bourse already.
Semper added that the listing commission meeting will be held next Tuesday but he was not sure whether it will discuss all applications.
Merko, one of Estonia's largest construction companies, has issued 722,705 new shares to raise its share capital to 29 million kroons. The issue closes on June 16.
It had a turnover of 209 million kroons and a net profit of 9.9 million kroons in 1996. Its net profit in the first quarter of 1997 was 5.1 million kroons.
Leks is the third largest non-life insurance company in Estonia. It had a net profit of four million kroons in 1996 and 2.8 million kroons in the first quarter of this year.
Its majority shares are held by Tallinna Pank , Estonia's fourth largest bank.
